actions.action: Inspect leaf undersides and stem joints with a flashlight for webbing, moving specks or stippling
Tap a branch over white paper to check for mites
Water thoroughly when dry and empty the saucer
Increase humidity with a pebble tray, humidifier or grouping plants
Move out of harsh direct sun and acclimate gradually if outdoors
Flush the soil to remove salt buildup
Trim dead leaf tips with clean scissors
Test neem/soap on one leaf and spray in shade early morning or evening
Keep treating mites if webbing or mites are found
Share close-up photos of leaf undersides and soil

reason: The answer treats watering and dry air as the main cause and mentions spider mites only as something to check. It just says to 'keep treating' mites if found, with no systemic insecticide. It isn't harmful, because it says to continue mite treatment if mites are confirmed.
